deviation_verdicts.committed_ai_sim_session_log: ACCEPT. A committed, reviewable log is preferable to per-run generation; determinism is proven by AiSession.test_generator_writes_the_committed_log (hashlib sha256, fixed strings, no randomness); matches how the other replay inputs are kept.
deviation_verdicts.refusal_codes_without_sub_reasons: ACCEPT. The design table names the codes; the 'As implemented' paragraph records it; the sub-reason stays available in markers for tests and the service; keeps the wire's reason vocabulary closed.
deviation_verdicts.ai_source_on_non_open_closes_nothing: ACCEPT. Table order puts ai_source first; there is nothing to close; tested in recSource and documented.
deviation_verdicts.ai_numeral_before_ai_markup: ACCEPT. Equivalent on parsable bodies (marker names hold no digit) and strictly more informative on unparsable ones; documented; tested ('[1]' -> ai_numeral). Nit: the table row still reads 'in the display text'; a two-word amendment ('in the body') would remove the double reading.
deviation_verdicts.descriptor_schema: ACCEPT. The design left the schema open; the chosen one (key, mime, bytes; width/height for images; duration_ms/segments_ms for voice; 4096 code points; extra fields echoed; variant excluded for voice) is documented in the design doc and pinned by 30+ fixtures and the record-mutants. The 4096 cap also bounds std/json decode on the strict VM.
deviation_verdicts.ci_about_20_minutes: ACCEPT. The PR run is 20m05s on x86_64; replay-compat adds about 40 s (session10k on VM + interpreter); the rest is pre-existing. TICKS=2000 is available if the PR-sized session should be used instead.
deviation_verdicts.ai4_fixtures_adapted_to_d21: ACCEPT. Required by D-21 (news 280) and the AI.4 evaluation's finding 5; minimal (2 request lines, 1 stub string); goldens re-recorded by make ai-stub-record with only lines 3 and 6 moving in each; the over_length stub stays over the cap (299 display chars).
